pages.text: The surface is a furnace: 464 degrees and 92 times Earth's air pressure, under a dim orange sky. Nothing you can build yet survives there for long.
Look at the land from above: folded tesserae, broad shield volcanoes and highlands frosted with metal that condenses out of the hot air like snow.

Climb into the cloud deck and the air cools and thins until, around the cloud tops, it is close to one bar and room temperature: the friendliest place in the solar system after Earth. But the clouds are sulfuric acid.
Venus turns backwards and very slowly: the sun rises in the west, and a day lasts months.
